new_value: Fixed in rust/lichen-core/src/loadng.rs. Investigation first: process_rreq() does NOT exist at HEAD and never existed in any commit of loadng.rs (git log --all -S process_rreq = empty; the bead was filed against a review snapshot that diverged from committed code). The actual RX entry point for received RREQs is Rreq::from_bytes, which accepted any hop_limit byte unvalidated — same amplification exposure via whatever consumes parsed RREQs. Fix: reject hop_limit > MAX_HOP_LIMIT(15) at parse with new LoadngError::HopLimitExceeded{got}, fail-closed so a forged RREQ can never re-enter propagation. Boundary semantics anchored to canonical vectors: hop_limit 0/4/15 parse OK (vectors rreq_zero_hop_limit/rreq_max_hop_limit), 16..=255 rejected (new tests rreq_hop_limit_above_max_rejected, rreq_hop_limit_boundaries_accepted). Verified: cargo test -p lichen-core --lib = 269 passed 0 failed; clippy clean for this module. Note: crate-wide clippy -D warnings gate has pre-existing unrelated failures, filed as project-LICHEN-worker6-u62c.
